correctness.rationale: In a topological ordering, consecutive runs from one shore give monochromatic blocks. Two vertices from the same shore lie in the same run exactly when all their cross-edge directions agree, and the relative order of the resulting runs is forced by the directions and alternating pattern. A nonconsecutive cross-edge has an alternative directed path through one vertex from each intermediate block, while a consecutive-block edge has no such path. Legal flips are therefore exactly the complete bipartite joins of consecutive blocks; assigning labels gives the multinomial weight. The undirected flips form a connected blow-up of a path. For m,n≥2 it is a tree exactly for sequences of length at least four with singleton interior blocks: two- and three-block sequences cannot be trees, and doubling an interior vertex creates a four-cycle. Even lengths give the symmetric falling-factorial sum; odd lengths require both ends on the larger shore and split its leftover labels into two nonempty end blocks, giving the second term. Stars have all edges flippable. For K_{2,n} a 2×n orientation matrix is acyclic exactly when at most one of the two mixed column types occurs. With j>0 mixed columns the flips number n+j, and with none they number 2n, giving the polynomial and coefficient. In the balanced case S_{n,n}<4(n!)² while the family with n−1 blocks per shore and one double block per shore gives at least (n!)²(n−1)²/2 orientations, proving the claimed decay. The graphical zonotope correspondence respects individual flips and degree.
residual_risks: The recorded finite matrix and block checks are corroboration only; the correctness conclusion rests on the unrestricted block, cycle, and counting arguments.
